column4: Returning the profile is modeled as emitting a fixed string to the html sink.
The language has no equality or comparison operator, so a password cannot be compared at all, let alone in constant time.
The success/error outcome is a public integer flag ok; the formatted response is a fixed literal.
No arrays or comparison: the block is one heap cell, and the slot count is always the fixed maximum (16) via a counted loop instead of min(count, max).
No parameter binding exists; the untrusted id is passed through san inside a quoted literal context instead.
No string inspection to test containment; the filename is sanitized with san before being joined to the base directory and sent to the fs sink.
The request method is a fixed literal; the user agent is the untrusted input passed through san.
Integers cannot be passed to a resource, so the token is held in a secret cell and the upstream call is modeled as check/access of resource upstream.
The session key is held in a secret cell and never used; the role flag is a public integer variable.
The downstream call is access downstream and the fixed delay is a 3-iteration skip loop; with no early exit, all 5 attempts always run.
The page size is the fixed cap (20) as a counted loop; offset cannot be expressed without arithmetic on indices and is omitted.
The hit/miss outcome is a public flag hit; writing to the cache is modeled as a second access cache.
The bounded job list is a 10-iteration counted loop over one resource job; the caller's per-job permission is a public flag allowed.
Parsing and normalization are modeled as storing a field count in the buffer and emitting the sanitized input.
The two failure points are public flags fail1 and fail2.
No arrays: each of 8 connection records is a cell allocated per loop iteration, and closing is logged then freed.
The two requests are modeled as one sequential program; storing the note is an access to resource notes plus a heap cell.
Per-cell counts are a single integer variable count; the result is stored in a heap cell since integers cannot be emitted.
No comparison operator: the range test outcome is a public flag inrange, and the typed error is a distinct literal.
No hash function: the hash is modeled as ( pw + salt ), stored in a secret cell and persisted via access creds.
No string comparison: matching the command name against the allowlist is modeled by public flags oprestart and opstatus; only fixed literals reach sh.
There are no byte buffers, string lengths or substring operations, so copying and truncating input to N bytes cannot be written.
The outcome of the authorization check is a public flag granted, and early return is modeled as the else branch.
The growable buffer is one heap cell whose stored length grows by chunk on each of 10 iterations.
The language has no equality or comparison operator, so the one-time code cannot be compared in constant time.
No string comparison or URL parsing: the allowlist match is a public flag hostallowed, the host is a fixed literal, and the path is sanitized; the sink is named location.
No comparison: the length-vs-capacity test is a public flag fits, and reading the body is a counted loop bounded by the 64-unit capacity.
The connection is a heap cell, and the mid-query error is a public flag err.
No functions: the helper is inlined as check report, and its success result is the flag ok.
No records: the name, role and quota fields are three separate heap cells, and ownership is a public flag owner.
Writing the trailing byte is modeled as storing an integer into the freed cell.
Integers cannot be emitted, so the response body is a public heap cell that receives the session key when verbose is set.
No comparison: the first-byte match is modeled as the sum ( secretbyte + guess ) used as the branch condition; the slow branch is a 100-iteration loop.
Finding the terminator is the public integer more, which is never updated, so the while loop has no bound.
